title: Far-Right France: Le Pen, Bardella, and the Future of Europe
gist: A review of Victor Mallet's book on France's Rassemblement National concludes that despite a lame-duck presidency and a hung parliament raising real odds of a far-right government, a Le Pen/Bardella-led France would govern with far less policy disruption — especially in foreign policy — than commonly assumed, because the party has moderated and is increasingly influenced by establishment money and media interests.

insights.claim: France currently has a lame-duck president and a hung parliament, creating a real near-term possibility of a far-right (Rassemblement National) victory in the next presidential election.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: France's political instability is a live tail risk for European policy continuity and euro-area governance that investors should monitor ahead of the next French presidential contest.
insights.quote: France has a lame-duck president, is toiling under a hung parliament, and faces the possibility of a far-right victory in the next election.

themes.theme: The moderation of the French far right

insights.claim: The Rassemblement National (formerly Front National) has moderated over time, and many of its remaining policy positions are economically impractical and thus likely to be abandoned should it take office.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: Suggests markets and policymakers may be overpricing disruption risk from a potential RN government; the party's actual governing agenda is likely narrower than its campaign rhetoric implies.
insights.quote: the Rassemblement National, the chief French far-right party formerly known as Front National, has moderated. Many of its remaining policy positions are economically impractical and thus likely to be abandoned should it enter office.

insights.claim: A Rassemblement National government would likely abandon its current rhetorical support for Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin because those positions have become severe political liabilities.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: Implies continuity in France's Atlanticist and anti-Russia posture even under a far-right government, reducing tail risk to EU-Russia sanctions policy and NATO cohesion.
insights.quote: it will doubtless eschew its support for U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin, positions that have become severe liabilities.

insights.claim: Establishment interests — monied backers, media tycoons, and moderate-right politicians, many of whom benefit from the globalization the party officially opposes — are increasingly influential within far-right French politics.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: This establishment capture reduces the odds of a genuinely disruptive anti-globalization policy agenda even under a far-right government, echoing a pattern seen in other European far-right parties.
insights.quote: Monied interests, media tycoons, and moderate-right politicians—many of whom are the beneficiaries of the globalization the party claims to oppose—loom larger in far-right politics.

insights.claim: A far-right French foreign policy is likely to differ less from the current French foreign policy than many observers expect, consistent with the pattern seen elsewhere in Europe.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: A useful contrarian baseline for scenario planning on EU cohesion and French foreign policy: markets should not assume a far-right win implies a foreign-policy break with Brussels or NATO.
insights.quote: As has been the case elsewhere in Europe, a far-right French foreign policy will differ less from the current one than many expect.
